This implies that the intake for N equilibrium (the requirement) will vary from 1.4 to 0.32 g kg1 d1 according to whether
energy intakes are low (equal to the resting metabolic rate RMR), or high, (equal to twice the RMR). In fact, most, (85%), of the
estimated between individual variability used to calculate the safe protein intake shown in Fig. 5 could be accounted for by an error
of only 10% of basal metabolic rate (BMR) in estimating the true energy needs of a subject (Millward, 2004, 2012a). Such errors
might not be observed in terms of weight change during the few days in which nitrogen balance is measured and it is likely that
many of the positive N-balances shown in Fig. 4 reﬂect excess energy intake.
Since N-balance varies as a function of energy intake, it may be argued that protein requirements can only be deﬁned in terms of
a speciﬁed energy intake level, but what is the appropriate energy intake? Should populations with low protein staples consume
